overview: This three-document file concerns an inquiry by the National Association of Broadcasters into the little-known Oriental Radio Association of Dairen, South Manchuria. Its managing director, James W. Baldwin, forwarded to Assistant Secretary of State R. Walton Moore a solicitation that a member broadcasting station had received from the association, which was collecting QRA cards for an exhibition connected with its forthcoming general meeting. After consulting within the State Department and with the Department of Commerce and Federal Communications Commission, the Department reported that it could find no information about the organization, speculated that it represented radio amateurs, and recommended contacting the American Radio Relay League.

subfiles.title: Baldwin asks Moore about the Oriental Radio Association
subfiles.from: James W. Baldwin, Managing Director, National Association of Broadcasters
subfiles.to: R. Walton Moore, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Baldwin requests information about the Oriental Radio Association in connection with an enclosed letter sent to a member broadcasting station.
subfiles.summary: James W. Baldwin forwards a letter addressed to one of the National Association of Broadcasters' member stations. He asks Assistant Secretary of State R. Walton Moore whether the Department possesses any information about the association that sent it. Departmental routing and receipt markings show that the inquiry was received and processed in late October 1936.

subfiles.title: Oriental Radio Association solicitation for QRA cards
subfiles.about: The Oriental Radio Association requests QRA cards for an exhibition planned alongside its winter general meeting in Dairen.
subfiles.summary: The Oriental Radio Association announces that its members will hold a general meeting in Dairen during the coming winter and plans an exhibition of radio-related material to take advantage of the gathering. It asks the recipient broadcasting station to contribute three or five copies of its QRA cards. The association also offers to furnish information about countries in its part of the world.

subfiles.title: State Department reply concerning the Oriental Radio Association
subfiles.from: R. Walton Moore, Assistant Secretary of State, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.to: James W. Baldwin, Managing Director, National Association of Broadcasters
subfiles.about: The Department reports that official inquiries produced no information about the Oriental Radio Association and suggests consulting the American Radio Relay League.
subfiles.summary: The State Department states that a careful internal inquiry, supplemented by consultations with the Department of Commerce and the Federal Communications Commission, failed to uncover information about the Dairen organization. The writer suspects that it may be an association of radio amateurs but emphasizes that this is uncertain. Baldwin is advised to contact Kenneth Warner of the American Radio Relay League in Hartford, Connecticut, for possible clarification.

interest: The file illustrates how an obscure international radio solicitation moved from a private broadcasting organization into an interagency federal inquiry. It is useful for studying amateur-radio networks, the circulation and collection of QRA cards, and American uncertainty about radio organizations operating in Japanese-controlled South Manchuria. The enclosure is especially revealing as direct evidence of the Oriental Radio Association's activities and its effort to cultivate contacts with foreign broadcasters.
